reviews.text: They've somehow managed the impossible and actually made things worse. I tried to connect my watch to my new phone and was met with a message saying it was no longer supported (S3 Frontier). Well, since they force you to disconnect from the old device and delete all of your data in order to pair the watch with a new one, and my old phone is broken, I now own a fancy paper weight that doesn't even function as a normal watch anymore. Thanks Samsung. The future looks great.

Won't even tell me why, no error codes, I've updated the app I don't know how many times, lost count of how many times I've uninstalled and reinstalled it just keeps me stuck on a loading screen for 30 minutes then just stops for no reason. On the very few times I've gotten it too connect to my phone, the connection lasts barely an hour before it disconnects.

You must turn on notifications in order to even open the app. I hate having any extra notifications on my phone. I do not want notifications for my watch popping up telling me it's done charging or whatever. I want to keep notifications off but if I do, I cannot even open the app up. My watch and my phone have also been disconnecting recently even though they're almost always in range of each other. The new update to how the workout tracking works was a big downgrade. It's messed up on two of my workouts, most recently randomly pausing most of my class before I realized. Even though it logged the whole time, it's only giving me data for the actively recorded portion and there's no way to manually override. The app no longer crashes and/or doesn't load forever. I also reset my watch (and backed it up) just to be sure. Hope this helps!

I Like my new phone! I like not having to carry my smartphone everywhere. I use it to send/receive texts, take phone calls, and access my emails. I don't know if I can send them too (I'm still learning how to use it). But as I've been learning, the Galaxy Watch does have some drawbacks: 1. It doesn't work in some buildings. I've found that unlike my smartphone it's paired too, the Galaxy Watch doesn't transmit as well, so there are dead zones in buildings that normally isn't there with a smartphone. But that's expected with a micro-transmitter, so I've gotten used to going outside at times. 2. Be careful with your apps and watchface you use. It drains the battery faster. I've learned to cut back on my apps by keeping only the apps that I need and not want. Since I did that, my watch lasts all day without having to turn on the power save function. I recommend shutting it off at night to conserve power, if you can. 3. Because of pairing, I don't get messages as quickly. So if my signal is week (i.e. inside a building), and you need something quick, think about where you are before you send or receive a text/call. Other than what's above, the benefits outweighs the drawbacks, and I highly recommend it!

This is addressed to anyone currently having issues with the Wearable app not working properly. I was having the same issues as you, and I went looking on the net to try and find solutions to the problem. Low and behold, Reddit has the fix.
